report_name: Block Inc. to Pay $45M in Settlement Over Cash App Security Failures

threat_actors.name: Unspecified Scammers on Cash App
threat_actors.description: Generic grouping of various scammers who exploited Cash App's inadequate security controls to conduct fraud, as described in the settlement between Block Inc. and 46 U.S. states. These actors used fraudulent accounts and social engineering scams to steal funds from users.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: Scammers conducted phishing and other social engineering scams, including fraudulent 'help line' scams and schemes related to 'Cash App Fridays' social media promotions, to defraud users.

attack_patterns.name: Create Account
attack_patterns.description: Scammers exploited Cash App's minimal identity verification processes to easily open fraudulent accounts for use in scams.

tools.name: Cash App
tools.description: A popular payment platform owned by Block, Inc. that was abused by scammers due to inadequate security safeguards and identity verification processes.

identities.name: Block, Inc.
identities.description: Parent company of Cash App that agreed to a $45 million settlement with 46 U.S. states for failing to adequately protect users from fraud and misrepresenting the security of its platform.

identities.name: Cash App Users
identities.description: Millions of users of the Cash App platform, particularly unbanked and underbanked consumers, who were vulnerable to scams and fraud due to the platform's security failures.

identities.name: Oregon Attorney General
identities.description: One of the leading state attorneys general in the multistate investigation and settlement with Block, Inc.

identities.name: Texas Attorney General
identities.description: One of the leading state attorneys general in the multistate investigation and settlement with Block, Inc. The state will receive nearly $5 million from the settlement.

identities.name: Virginia Attorney General
identities.description: A participating state attorney general in the settlement with Block, Inc. The state will receive approximately $845,500.

identities.name: Colorado Attorney General
identities.description: A participating state attorney general in the settlement with Block, Inc. The state will receive over $1.6 million.

identities.name: Illinois Attorney General
identities.description: A participating state attorney general in the settlement with Block, Inc.

identities.name: Tennessee Attorney General
identities.description: A participating state attorney general in the settlement with Block, Inc.

infrastructure.name: Fraudulent Customer Support Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Fraudulent 'help line' scams created by third parties to impersonate Cash App customer support and defraud users, filling the vacuum left by the company's lack of live phone support.
